data.narrative:
Mesh Optical Technologies is a Series A-stage semiconductor company that has raised $50M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 11 peers: 3 public semiconductor companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage competitors including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor.

A single valuation method proved applicable: stage-progression analysis. Using total capital raised ($50M) as a proxy for current value, a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $100M. This method is grounded in the observation that early-stage venture capital deployed typically commands a markup upon subsequent financing rounds. Peer-median analysis could not be applied due to insufficient comparable data points within narrow stage and valuation bands—while 12 same-sector peers exist, filtering by stage and tier produced fewer than three comparable transactions. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (median 21.4x across the three public semiconductors) cannot be applied because private company revenue is not on file.

The triangulated range is $85M–$115M, with a median of $100M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single method and carries material uncertainty around the appropriate stage-progression multiplier for optical semiconductor hardware. Key downside risks include competitive intensity within advanced optics and execution risk common to early-stage chip companies. Upside scenarios depend on proprietary differentiation and pathway to revenue scale.
